transcript:
amy: Heads-up — onboarding gptx-small-v1. Seeing tokenization deltas between HF tokenizer and our runtime when using chat templates. Also weights uploaded to s3://rw-models/gptx-small/v1/weights.tar.gz — can infra confirm checksum before we flip traffic?

raj: I can check checksum. Can you paste a minimal repro for the tokenizer mismatch? quick example of what's failing helps.

amy: gist of it: when we run the chat template (system -> user -> assistant) huggingface tokenizer adds a BOS token only for system messages, our runtime pipeline doesn't. That shifts KV cache indexing and causes early truncation in long chats.

marco: ugh. Do we know which tokenizer type this model uses? sentencepiece vs byte-level-bpe vs tokenizers? different libs sometimes handle <|system|> style markers differently.

amy: model bundle has tokenizer type = "sentencepiece" in metadata. quick repro I ran locally:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("/tmp/gptx-small-v1-tokenizer")
# chat template: [SYSTEM]<msg>[USER]<msg>
print(tok.encode("<|system|> System prompt\n<|user|> Hello", add_special_tokens=True))
# output: [101, 2, ...]  # bos present before system only
```

sophia: interesting. Our serving runtime has had an implicit "strip_bos_for_role_templates" optimization on some chat paths to reduce token count. That could explain the mismatch.

lee: infra-bot: checksum request for s3://rw-models/gptx-small/v1/weights.tar.gz
infra-bot: CHECKSUM OK — md5: a7c3f9b2d1e2c6b8d4f9e0c3f1b2a9d0

raj: thanks. For tokenizer check: amy, can you run a small validation script that compares three things and paste output: (1) HF encode with add_special_tokens=True, (2) HF encode without special tokens, (3) runtime tokenizer output for same string. We need token ids and token count.

amy: done, pasted below (shortened):
- hf_with:  [101, 50256, 345, ... 2]
- hf_no:    [50256, 345, ...]
- runtime:  [50256, 345, ...]

observation: HF inserted a BOS-like id (101) before system only. runtime and hf_no match after that, so the delta is a single leading token on system messages.

marco: OK that's actionable — two options: (A) make runtime mirror HF and add BOS for system messages, or (B) normalize HF outputs by stripping leading BOS before comparing/cache indexing. Which is safer for existing apps?

sophia: A is safer for forward-compatibility but risk: increases token counts & cost. B is riskier if HF model expects BOS present for some behaviors.

lee: quick config suggestion: add explicit flags to model_config.json so serving behavior is deterministic:

```json
{
  "bos_token_id": 101,
  "eos_token_id": 2,
  "pad_token_id": 0,
  "inject_bos_for_roles": ["system"],
  "normalize_input_tokens": false
}
```

amy: +1 to explicit flags. I've opened a tiny PR in infra-configs to set inject_bos_for_roles for gptx-small-v1 to ["system"], and added a unit test that tokenizes the canonical chat template and asserts stable kv cache offsets.

raj: pinged code owners on the PR. Can someone from runtime validate the change won't break batching logic? marco?

marco: I'll run the runtime integration job tomorrow AM. Quick things to watch: batch scheduler assumes consistent sequence lengths across roles in prefix caching; adding BOS only for system could make sequences non-uniform. We'll add a normalizer step in the batching path to keep lengths aligned if needed.

sophia: also check prompt formatting docs — add a note in docs/chat-templates.md that some models require explicit BOS on specific roles and that this is configurable via model_config.

amy: noted, I'll add doc blurb in the PR.

lee: infra-bot: deployed checksum-verified weights to staging path s3://rw-models/gptx-small/v1/staging/
infra-bot: staged

marco: quick status: I'll run integration tests against staging weights + config change. ETA ~ 12h. If green, we can promote to dedicated-canary and watch latency/cost delta.

amy: thanks all — small follow-ups: (1) raj — please approve the config PR once checksum confirmed (done), (2) marco — post test log in this thread, (3) sophia — doc blurb review. I'll schedule a very short async update in #eng-ml tomorrow.

sophia: reviewing doc blurb now :thumbsup:

raj: approved the PR.

marco: quick update — integration job passed basic kv-cache tests. saw ~0.4% token increase for chat-only flows when inject_bos_for_roles=["system"], latency unchanged. pushing to canary now.

amy: perfect. keep an eye on regressions and evals (I've added an automated eval comparing top-1 completions before/after). If anything odd, rollback to normalized-mode.

lee: noted. closing out on infra side unless y'all need more.

amy: awesome, thanks everyone :rocket:
